tasks.short: Supervise engineering student teaching, internships and research.

steps.what: Define the supervision question and independent checks for the student's engineering model
Run the student's submitted model against benchmarks in an isolated engineering environment
Review physical assumptions, engineering reasoning and the meaning of benchmark results
Supervise the student's work and challenge reasoning in discussion
Write and approve the supervision record and student action note
Commit the approved supervision record
Send the approved engineering action note to the supervised student

tasks.design: For computational engineering supervision, configure the native batch runner in {OTHER}, the isolated engineering modelling environment. The teacher defines independent checks and interprets physics and results. Preserve discussion and record writing. Commit the final supervision record and send the separately checked student note through distinct native {LMS} actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: A model producing numbers does not establish sound engineering assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch execution can run explicit benchmark cases without repeating hands-on launches.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing informative checks and evaluating physical validity remain expert work.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what the student understands and challenge a plausible but physically wrong result.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated benchmark launching and record transfer; supervision judgement stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: engineering solvers can batch explicit cases in an isolated environment; interpreting correctness still requires the supervisor.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for a computational research supervision case, not all teaching or internships. Only hands-on repeated test launches qualify; solver runtime and existing batch automation do not.

s1 teacher produces case_id, input_values, units, expected_result, tolerance and resource_limit. Benchmark design/capture remains full time. Student supplies model_version and documented entry point; missing cases or unsafe dependencies return to manual review, not unrestricted execution.

s2 has no network or physical-rig control and no production credentials. s3 retains full review of units, boundary conditions and independence of the benchmark. A passing comparison is not automatic academic acceptance.

s5 teacher captures observation, action, owner and due_date, writing separate private and student-facing versions. a1/a2 bind those actual final versions, destination and recipient after s5; edits revoke approval. Validate actual separate save/send work before claiming it.
research_questions: Which repeated execution actions can the native runner remove without weakening independent model review?

incremental.description: Maintain sandbox dependencies and supervision routing

approvals.approved_version: s5 final supervision record and restricted LMS destination
s5 final student action note and student recipient

tasks.short: Stay current through engineering literature, colleagues and professional conferences.

steps.what: Choose engineering topics, journals and conference themes relevant to teaching and research
Retrieve and select current literature through native library database alerts
Read current literature and assess methods, evidence and relevance
Talk with colleagues about new engineering findings and practical implications
Participate in professional conference sessions and technical exchanges
Write and check personal notes linking developments to their original sources
Save the checked personal engineering development notes

tasks.design: Configure saved searches and a native results view in {OTHER}, the institution's licensed engineering literature database. The teacher still selects papers, reads them, talks with colleagues and attends conferences. Keep personal note writing and save as explicit full-time steps; no model summary substitutes for reading.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring searches can repeat manual navigation, while judging engineering developments requires reading the underlying work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches can present new metadata matching explicit topics and dates.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing methods, applicability and contradictory evidence remains scholarship.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a methodological advance that changes teaching or research practice.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated search navigation, with learning and interaction preserved.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: scholarly databases provide saved searches and new-result views without requiring generated summaries.

assumptions: Provisional shares include literature, colleague exchange, conference participation and personal notes. No reduced reading time or new report baseline is assumed.

s1 teacher supplies query_terms, journal_scope, date_window and topic_exclusions, counting setup and interpretation there. Publishers/library supply title, author, publication_date and resolvable_identifier. Missing metadata is checked manually in retained s2 time.

s2 retains 9 hours for title/abstract selection and source resolution. Native alerts are configured as an in-app view, not a new mail send. If saved searches are already used, there is no new navigation gain.

s6 captures source_reference, finding, limitation and possible_application; note writing and single save stay full. a1 binds that actual final note after its check. No colleague or conference labour is claimed as displaced.
research_questions: Does a saved query surface relevant new work while preserving deliberate exploration beyond its terms?

incremental.description: Tune saved queries as research questions change

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver engineering lectures on mechanics, hydraulics or robotics.

steps.what: Choose lecture objectives and an appropriate sequence of engineering concepts
Derive worked examples and specify physical assumptions, equations and parameter ranges
Produce example figures using native engineering calculation and plotting tools
Prepare the lecture deck with a native reusable teaching template
Check derivations, units, figures and accessibility; approve the final lecture package
Deliver the lecture and respond to student questions and misunderstandings
Publish the approved lecture materials to the enrolled students

tasks.design: Use native plotting in {OTHER}, the engineering calculation environment, for teacher-derived examples and a reusable {DOCS} lecture template. Preserve derivation, figure interpretation, final checks and the full live lecture. Publish the actual approved package through a separate gated {LMS} action.
tasks.previous_blocker: An attractive figure or slide does not establish correct mechanics or a good explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plotting and slide templates can reuse explicit equations and parameter sets.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing revealing examples and responding to student misconceptions remain teaching work.
tasks.human_edge: Connect mathematical form to physical meaning in a way the class understands.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated figure and slide formatting; unchanged teaching and derivation time.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native calculation plots and presentation templates can assist lecture preparation without generating physical reasoning.

assumptions: Provisional shares describe a lecture with worked examples and figures. Confirm current manual plotting, formatting and upload work; existing native automation gives no new saving. Software compute time is excluded.

s2 teacher supplies equation, units, boundary_conditions, parameter_name, parameter_values and expected_limit; derivation and input capture stay full. s3 retains 4 hours for figure selection, labels and interpretation. Missing or invalid parameters return to manual example preparation.
s4 retains substantive text and narrative changes; only repeated template layout is shortened. No model writes equations or chooses engineering assumptions.

s5 approves the actual completed figures, solutions, slides and audience. a1 binds package hashes, course_id and cohort; revisions during delivery require checking the changed final package before publication. No automatic follow-up mail is introduced.
research_questions: Which repeated figure/layout actions remain after the teacher's existing calculation and presentation tools?

incremental.description: Maintain example plotting templates and LMS package mapping

approvals.approved_version: s5 final checked lecture package, course and cohort

tasks.short: Initiate, facilitate and moderate engineering class discussions.

steps.what: Choose a discussion problem that exposes important engineering assumptions
Initiate the class discussion and invite alternative engineering explanations
Facilitate and moderate discussion, probing reasoning and balancing participation
Explain the discussion's conclusions and unresolved engineering questions aloud
Write and check the brief class discussion summary in the course workspace
Publish the checked discussion summary to the class

tasks.design: Retain live questioning, moderation and oral synthesis. Separate the brief written summary and final publication in {LMS}. Evaluate the existing native course-note template and publish control first; for a short note already entered once in that workspace, no additional mechanism is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: A useful discussion depends on hearing student reasoning and responding to it in the moment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing LMS notes already handle the small written artefact in this scenario.
tasks.still_hard: Participation, productive disagreement and correcting physical misconceptions need a teacher.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a question that reveals why a student believes a physically impossible answer.
tasks.altitude: No demonstrated saving after separating summary writing and publication.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live class moderation remains interpersonal teaching, and native course notes can already capture a short summary once.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for an engineering discussion with a brief course note; no student time is counted as displaced. Oral and written synthesis are separate steps.
s5 teacher captures topic, accepted_conclusion, assumption_limits and unresolved_question directly after discussion. No transcript, automatic speaker record or duplicated report baseline is assumed.

Native templates and publication are explicitly assessed. The short summary still needs its teacher-authored engineering meaning; an added drafting loop has no demonstrated net benefit after capture/checking. Existing direct publication is retained at full time.
a1 binds the actual final summary and class audience after s5; edits require a new check. No additional software or recurring maintenance is introduced.
research_questions: Is there an actual duplicated writing or send action beyond the brief native summary represented here?

incremental.description: No new system; retain native course notes and publish control

approvals.approved_version: s5 final checked discussion summary and class audience

role.altitude: Keep engineering reasoning and live teaching central while reducing explicit computational and document operations.
reach: Help student project teams define independent model checks and traceable worked examples.
role.ambitious_version: An engineering teacher who uses reliable tools for repeated operations and spends teaching time exposing students' assumptions.
